items.title: Market Selloff Hits Financial Stocks. Why Banks, Brokerages Are Caught in the Crossfire.
items.summary: Shares of financial services companies as varied as Robinhood, Webull, Goldman Sachs, and Morgan Stanley fell sharply on Thursday.

items.title: Morgan Stanley Sinks 6%, Goldman Down 6%, Citi Down 5% as Market Selloff Drags Wall Street Banks
items.summary: Key TakeawaysMorgan Stanley fell 6% today, with Goldman Sachs and Citigroup down about as much, in a broad selloff with no company news behind it. Morgan Stanley leans on trading far more than JPMorgan Chase, which leaves it among the banks most exposed if trading and dealmaking cool.

items.summary: In a shift from previous years, the bank didn’t provide a gender or racial breakdown of the class.

items.title: Is a Gold Bullion ETF a Better Investment Than a Silver Miners Fund? ETFs from Goldman Sachs and iShares Battle It Out
items.summary: Physical gold offers lower costs and less volatility, while mining stocks deliver higher dividend income. Both delivered nearly identical $2,200 returns on $1,000 invested over five years.

items.title: Could Uber Actually Climb 61%? Or Is Goldman Sachs Totally Wrong?
items.summary: Key TakeawaysGoldman Sachs reiterated its Buy rating and $110 price target on Uber on Nov. 5, about 61% above today’s price, after a fifth straight quarter of at least 20% bookings growth.

items.title: Wall Street Is Being Asked to Take Part of SpaceX’s $40 Billion AI Bet
items.summary: Goldman Sachs and Apollo are reportedly shopping pieces of SpaceX's AI chip financing to investors, and whoever signs up inherits a risk the company refuses to carry. The real question is how fast newer silicon erodes the value of the hardware.

items.title: Voters Just Made Microsoft’s Data Centers More Valuable, a Wall Street Veteran Says
items.summary: Microsoft hit a record after voters turned against local data center projects, but the same limits that make its existing capacity scarcer could also throttle the build-out behind Azure's growth. Which way does the risk cut for shareholders?
